text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - Cash debt and futures prices continued to track sideways in firmer ground during late trading, with dealers saying the outlook for the next few sessions had a light positive edge to it. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.97, up 0.17 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK government bonds outperformed Bunds in a thin trading session, with prices buoyed by relatively weak producer price figures for March. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 108-30/32, up 11/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures erased their losses on Monday to finish slightly firmer in thin volume ahead of release of the U.S. consumer price index aUSCPI on Tuesday. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.24, up 0.02 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds futures showed extended gains by late afternoon buoyed by the hopes of an official interest rate cut on the back of falling inflation while the firmer lira also helped contracts, dealers said. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 128.26, up 0.98 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury securities prices remained tightly range bound at midday as players had little new information to trade upon. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 106-20/32, unchanged from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.17 percent.

JAPAN - Key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures ended lower after extending losses toward the close due to position-adjustment sales and as Tokyo share prices came off the day's lows. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 126.48, down 0.16 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - After a dearth of 10-year dollar paper, the European Investment Bank (EIB) filled the gap with a $500 million 10-year offering on Monday. The bond was priced to yield 18 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes via joint lead managers Goldman Sachs and SBC Warburg. Dealers away from the lead said the bond was priced "on the tight side". A syndicate official said while the deal did not achieve "blow-out status", there was buoyant demand from Asia. "The EIB is an eye-catching name," he said.
